title: Order checkout failing
executive_summary: INC-007 (SEV2): order checkout error rate exceeded 25%. Symptom start is 15:25Z per the incident record. Final status is INCONCLUSIVE, so the root cause could not be established. The leading hypothesis, H1, is that config cfg-7f81d14a (order-service payment_client.timeout_ms 3000 -> 300, applied 15:22:00Z under OPS-2375) causes order-service to abort POST /v1/charges calls that exceed 300ms. This has the best timing fit: the first "timed out after 300ms" error is at 15:23:20Z (logpat-order-service-f003ad98), and order-service timeout_rate rises from a baseline of 0.1 to a window mean of 23.54 with onset at 15:23:00Z (met-order-service-timeout_rate-1520-1530). The mechanism is not verified. Payment-side p95 (about 151ms) and p99 (about 300ms) do not show the latency rise needed to explain a roughly 35% timeout rate (met-payment-service-p95_latency_ms-1515-1540, met-payment-service-p99_latency_ms-1455-1550). H1 confidence is 0.43 with status needs_evidence. H3 (payment 5.8.1 deploy) is rejected. H2 (path-level loss between services) is weakened but not excluded.

hypotheses.description: Config cfg-7f81d14a (order-service payment_client.timeout_ms 3000 -> 300, OPS-2375) applied at 15:22Z makes order-service abort POST /v1/charges calls to payment-service that take longer than 300ms, producing the checkout error spike. Payment-side arrivals falling after 15:24 is plausibly a downstream effect of the order-side circuit breaker opening at 15:24:10Z. Mechanism: timeout_ms lowered 10x (3000->300) -> order-side client cancels payment charge calls at 300ms -> PaymentClient timeout ERRORs from 15:23:20Z, error/timeout rate step at 15:23 bucket (~29-35%) -> failure ratio 0.64 opens payment circuit breaker 15:24:10Z -> retry budget exhausted 15:25:13Z -> checkout failures surfaced in order-service (gateway unchanged) -> payment receives fewer charge calls (short-circuited) from ~15:25.
confidence_explanation: +0.08 proposed cause (15:22) precedes/coincides with first observed anomaly (15:23)

critic_review.summary: H1 (order-service payment_client.timeout_ms 3000->300, cfg-7f81d14a) is the leading hypothesis. Its timing is strong: the config lands at 15:22Z, the first 'timed out after 300ms' ERROR is at 15:23:20Z, and no timeouts appear before that. The error/timeout step at the 15:23 bucket matches. However, the mechanism is quantitatively unverified. Payment-side p95 is flat at ~151ms and p99 is ~300ms in baseline, so only a small share of calls should exceed 300ms. A ~35% timeout rate at a 300ms cutoff requires a large share of calls to take >300ms, which payment-side latency does not show. Either the latency is added on the order side or the path, or the mechanism is different. H3 is rejected: order error rate is flat from 14:40 to 15:20, payment latency and errors are flat, and all timeouts cite the order-side 300ms setting. H2 is weakened: order timeouts start at 15:23:20Z, before the 15:25 payment arrival drop, so the drop cannot be the initial cause. The path-level telemetry needed to test H2 is also not obtainable with current tools. The breaker/retry logs are downstream consequences, not causes. Requested: order-service p50/p95 latency and timeout_rate at 1-minute resolution for 15:15-15:35 to see whether the 300ms cutoff is reached by a large fraction of calls. Also requested: config/deploy records for order-service per instance at 15:22Z to confirm the timeout value was applied everywhere. This is the final round, so if the latency check cannot be run, the H1 conclusion should be reported as likely but not fully proven.

assessments.reasoning: Strong timing match (config 15:22Z, timeouts from 15:23:20Z, none before) and the error/timeout step is on the exact changed path. But payment p95 ~151ms and p99 ~300ms in baseline and flat in the window do not explain a ~35% rate of calls exceeding 300ms. Need order-side latency distribution and per-instance config application to close the gap.

The payment arrival drop at 15:25 is 1-2 minutes after order timeouts begin at 15:23:20Z, so it cannot be the initial cause. Only metric support exists (single source). Payment error and timeout rates are flat. Path telemetry is not available to the team, so H2 is weak and cannot be confirmed as the root cause.

conclusion: Root cause could not be conclusively established with the available evidence. The root cause of INC-007 could not be established, and the investigation is INCONCLUSIVE. The most likely explanation is the order-service payment timeout reduction (cfg-7f81d14a, 3000 -> 300ms), based on close timing alignment with the error onset. The quantitative mechanism is unverified: payment-side latency is flat, and it is not shown that enough calls exceed 300ms to produce the observed timeout rate. H3 is rejected. H2 and order-side added latency remain open. Priorities are rollback of the timeout change and collection of the order-side latency and outbound-count data needed to close the evidence gaps.
